tiles.name: 2.45 GHz filter
tiles.result: 1.7 dB of loss from 2.4 to 2.5 GHz, 30 dB or more below 2.2 GHz and above 2.7 GHz (the datasheet); 50 ohm in and out
notes: Murata LFB212G45SG8A127, a 2012-size LTCC band-pass.  The line to each jack is 50 ohm coplanar waveguide (0.29 mm
wide, 0.25 to the ground pour) with a via fence; the jack's centre pin has no plane under it (a 2.2 mm void).
Sweep it with the synthesizer R10 or R11 into a power meter, or with a DAC harmonic comb and the ADC.

tiles.name: 915 MHz filter
tiles.result: 1.1 dB of loss from 902 to 928 MHz, 40 dB or more 30 MHz outside the band (the datasheet); 50 ohm in and out
notes: RF360 B39921B2672P810: a surface-acoustic-wave filter for the 915 MHz ISM band, 26 MHz wide, in a 1411 package;
its skirts are much steeper than the LTCC's.  Lines, fences and launch voids as on R2.

tiles.name: gain block
tiles.subtitle: GALI-84+
tiles.result: 20 dB of gain from 50 MHz to 2.5 GHz (datasheet: 21.9 dB at 1 GHz, 1 dB compression at +20 dBm out); 97 mA from 7.8 V
notes: Mini-Circuits GALI-84+: a Darlington MMIC that sets its own current; the 22 ohm from the 7.8 V rail drops to its
5.8 V device voltage (0.2 W in the 2512).  The 27 nH choke (415 ohm at 2.45 GHz, 155 at 915 MHz) feeds the
output pin; 100 pF blocks keep the DC off the jacks.  Keep the input under 0 dBm for linear gain.  The slide
switch and P-FET gate the tile's 7.8 V as on AMOD-A.

tiles.name: power
tiles.subtitle: USB-C 5 V in: +5, +7.8 V; 25 MHz reference
tiles.result: +5 V from the USB-C (up to 1.5 A), +7.8 V at 250 mA for the gain blocks (yellow LED), a 25 MHz square wave on REF OUT
notes: USB-C power only: 5.1 k on each CC asks any source for 5 V; a 2 A PTC, a 5 V TVS and 20 uF.  The MT3608 boosts to 7.8 V
(0.6 V x 13 from 12 k / 1 k) for the two GALI-84+ tiles (200 mA); the +8V rail is a strip under row 1 that their
headers reach with a via.  The TPS7A2033 makes 3.3 V for the TC32H4 TCXO (+-2 ppm) and the 74LVC1G17 that drives
REF OUT (51 ohm: 1.6 Vpp into 50 ohm, 3.3 Vpp into a synthesizer's unterminated REF IN; a tee feeds both synthesizers).
The TCXO's pad 1 (enable or no connection on the drawing) floats, as CostasLink's review settled.

tiles.name: synthesizer
tiles.subtitle: MAX2871
tiles.result: any frequency from 23.5 MHz to 6 GHz on OUT A (-4 to +5 dBm in steps), locked to the 25 MHz on REF IN; the red LED says locked
notes: MAX2871 as CostasLink built it: fractional-N PLL with four VCOs, programmed over SPI from the Pmod (SCLK, SDATA,
LE; MUXOUT back).  The loop filter is third order, 80-120 kHz with 61 degrees of margin for both 915 MHz (VCO / 4)
and 2.4 GHz (VCO / 2) at ICP 2.56 mA (RSET 5.1 k, CP = 7).  RFOUTA+ feeds the jack through 27 nH to 3.3 V and
100 pF; RFOUTA- is terminated in 51 ohm the same way; RFOUTB is open and must stay disabled.  CE and RFOUT_EN are
tied high, LE has 100 k down.  REF IN is unterminated: one REF OUT drives both synthesizers through a tee.
